doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: What Berklee gave her beyond the classical path in Israel
summary: Asked about a classical career in Israel, she says Berklee opened her to an international community and varied music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: If you had stayed in the classical realm in Israel, can you surmise that you might have been able to make a living in that genre? Without coming to America?

I don’t know. I don’t really know. In any kind of music I mean I went to study, I went to college, I went to Berklee College of Music and of course there’s all the curriculum and the academic world and the subjects that I studied, but I think that the main important thing that Berklee gave me is opening the door to the international community and through the people, the other students, expand my horizons and really fall in love with a variety of music that maybe if I stayed in Israel it would have taken me longer to get to. Of course the internet arrived a little later, so it was not like today with the press of a button you’re like, you travel the world. And you look at the world through Google and you can just look at the streets and drive around and listen to music and have radio stations that play music from any era and every point in the world. It wasn’t as easy.
